title: Drop the tax on foreign sovereign investors
name: Drop the tax on foreign sovereign investors
noun: dropping the tax on foreign sovereigns
headline: Drop sovereign investor tax. Costs £0.7bn in 2029-30.
description: From January 2029 foreign states investing in UK property pay tax on that income and those gains, under a new statutory regime. Switch this on to drop it and give up what the Treasury scores for it.

baselinePolicy.text: A statutory regime taxes foreign sovereigns’ UK real estate income and gains from 1 January 2029 (Table 6.1 line 54).

source.quote: primarily bringing certain real estate income and gains into UK tax

alreadyIncludes: A statutory regime taxes foreign sovereigns’ UK real estate income and gains from 1 January 2029 (Table 6.1 line 54).

lines.title: Modernising Taxation of Foreign Sovereign Investments: Introduce a new statutory regime for the direct taxation of foreign sovereigns from 1 January 2029

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
The OBR rates this costing as highly uncertain: how much sovereign investment is in scope, and how it responds, is not well known (October 2026 outlook, Table 3.3).

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
